body.statement:
For the full-design-centered subclass \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), the full-data interval \(C_\alpha\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies, along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\),
\[
\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Moreover, for constants \(0<c_\alpha<C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\),
\[
c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}
\le
\inf_{I:\,\text{uniformly conditionally honest over }\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\]
Coverage is obtained by conditioning on the complete historical design, \(E_0\), and donors; applying bounded cluster-level Hoeffding bounds separately to the historical and event sums; applying the exact Taylor allowance and donor fourth-moment calibration; and using Bonferroni.  The result requires neither temporal independence within a unit, studentization, a dense-local-site condition, nor sequential overlap.  The log-adjusted spacing term is uniform and unavoidable under the maintained geometric beta-mixing and marginal-density assumptions.
body.justification: The full-data interval combines exact bounded-cluster calibration with explicit Taylor and donor allowances and matches the four-channel lower bound.
body.gap: No block multiplier, studentization, dense-site condition, or event conditional-variance premise is used.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain uniformly conditionally honest intervals with optimal expected length at every phase boundary.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  Polynomial reproduction on every successful fit gives
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{stik}p(u_{stk})=p(0)
\]
for every polynomial \(p\) of total degree at most \(r\).  Apply this identity to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_{sk}\).  The Holder remainder then gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_{sk}
-m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
-\sum_{t,i}a_{stik}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{22}
\]
After weighting cohorts and averaging folds, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} gives conditional mean zero, and conditional cross-unit independence makes the \(U_{si}\) independent over \((s,i)\) under the displayed conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|.
\]
If a centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its conditional moment generating function by the endpoint mixture with the same mean; elementary one-variable differentiation of that mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\]
Multiplication over independent units, Chernoff's inequality, and optimization in \(v\) therefore give
\[
P\!\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{23}
\]

Similarly define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\right\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers these variables conditional on \((\mathscr X,E_0)\).  They are independent across units and have range lengths at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation gives
\[
P\!\left(
\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{24}
\]
No independence between a unit's event outcome and its historical path is invoked: (23) and (24) will be combined by Bonferroni.

For donor fold \(k\), put \(m=m_k\) and \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\).  Donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors with \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding the fourth power and retaining precisely the index patterns in which every centered vector occurs at least twice yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P\left[
\left\|m^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
&=m^{-1}\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1m\right)
\left\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\right\}\\
&\le \frac Bm+\left(1-\frac1m\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
\]
Markov's inequality at \(q_k\) gives conditional error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}/K_D\) for this fold.  Euclidean projection onto the closed cube is nonexpansive because, coordinate by coordinate, truncation to \([0,1]\) cannot increase distance from the point \(z_0\) already in the cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds then imply, on the calibrated event,
\[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\left\{\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0\right\}
\right\|_2
\le \sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,\frac{q_k}{\sqrt{m_k}}
=\delta_k.
\tag{26}
\]
A union bound over folds has total error at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\).  On the good sample \(\delta_k\le\delta_0\); hence the upper local-modulus inequality and (26) give
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_k^\kappa.
\tag{27}
\]
Averaging (27) over folds gives \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).

By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the error of the full-data raw estimator is the event fluctuation in (24), minus the historical fluctuation in (23), minus the Taylor remainder in (22), minus the generated-center discrepancy in (27).  Bonferroni and
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}+
\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha
\]
show that, on the good sample,
\[
P\{|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\le H_\alpha\mid E_0\}
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]
On the bad sample the interval is \([-B,B]\), and \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) by bounded event wealth.  Thus (28) proves the asserted uniform conditional coverage.  Notice that it uses neither studentization nor any lower conditional-variance assumption for event outcomes.

We next bound expected length.  The deterministic conclusion of \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\sqrt{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\sqrt{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}}.
\tag{29}
\]
The kernel support and the same weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_kh_{sk}^\lambda.
\]
The bandwidth moment in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control}, now with exponent \(\lambda\), implies
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{30}
\]
Because \(D,S,K_D\) are fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\), (25) makes \(q_k\) uniformly bounded, whence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}
=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{31}
\]
By the selector-control lemma, the bad-sample probability is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  The fallback interval has length at most \(2B\), and \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\) eventually.  Equations (29)--(31), together with \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on the good sample, prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{32}
\]

For the matching lower bound, reduce the fixed perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so that every channel affinity \(A_q\) is greater than \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\).  This is also possible for the rare-block pair by reducing its active-block intensity while retaining a fixed positive separation constant.  Let \(I\) be uniformly conditionally \((1-\alpha)\)-honest, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\).  Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge \mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
On the event in (33), \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge\Delta_q\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0\Delta_q
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\]
Maximizing over the four channels gives the lower bound
\(c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Together with (28) and (32), this proves the same-class expected-length bracket in every relative-growth regime.
